title: Sun
d: The Sun holds 99.86 percent of all mass in the solar system, fusing 600 million tons of hydrogen every second. Its light takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach ...
description: The Sun holds 99.86 percent of all mass in the solar system, fusing 600 million tons of hydrogen every second. Its light takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth, and its planets, dwarf planets, moons, and comets are all bound by its gravity. type: G-type main-sequence star. diameter: 1,392,700 km. note: 99.86 percent of the system mass; fusion of hydrogen powers everything..

facts.note: 99.86 percent of the system mass; fusion of hydrogen powers everything.

title: Mercury
d: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun, racing around it in just 88 days. With almost no atmosphere, its surface swings from -180 C at nig...
description: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun, racing around it in just 88 days. With almost no atmosphere, its surface swings from -180 C at night to 430 C by day, and its cratered face resembles the Moon. diameter: 4,879 km. distance: 0.39 AU. day: 59 Earth days. year: 88 days. moons: 0. note: Smallest planet; huge temperature swings..

title: Venus
d: Venus is wrapped in a crushing carbon-dioxide atmosphere that traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect, making it the hottest planet at 465 C. It spins back...
description: Venus is wrapped in a crushing carbon-dioxide atmosphere that traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect, making it the hottest planet at 465 C. It spins backwards, so slowly that its day outlasts its year. diameter: 12,104 km. distance: 0.72 AU. day: 243 days (retrograde). year: 225 days. moons: 0. note: Hottest planet; crushing CO2 atmosphere..

title: Earth
d: Earth is the only known planet with life, liquid-water oceans covering 71 percent of its surface, and an oxygen atmosphere. Its magnetic field and ozone laye...
description: Earth is the only known planet with life, liquid-water oceans covering 71 percent of its surface, and an oxygen atmosphere. Its magnetic field and ozone layer shield the biosphere, and its single large Moon steadies its seasons. diameter: 12,742 km. distance: 1 AU. day: 24 hours. year: 365.25 days. moons: 1. note: The only known world with life..

facts.note: The only known world with life.

title: Mars

description: Mars hosts Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the solar system at nearly 22 km, and Valles Marineris, a canyon that would span the United States. Ancient riverbeds show water once flowed; today robots roam its rusty deserts. diameter: 6,779 km. distance: 1.52 AU. day: 24.6 hours. year: 687 days. moons: 2. note: Olympus Mons; dusty red deserts..

title: Jupiter

description: Jupiter is the giant of the solar system, more massive than all other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth that has raged for centuries, and its 95 moons include four planet-sized Galilean worlds. diameter: 139,820 km. distance: 5.2 AU. day: 9.9 hours. year: 11.9 years. moons: 95. note: Largest planet; Great Red Spot storm..

facts.note: Largest planet; Great Red Spot storm.

title: Saturn

description: Saturn is famous for its dazzling rings — billions of ice and rock particles spanning 280,000 km yet only about 10 meters thick. It is the least dense planet and leads the system with 146 confirmed moons. diameter: 116,460 km. distance: 9.5 AU. day: 10.7 hours. year: 29.4 years. moons: 146. note: Famous rings of ice and rock..

facts.note: Famous rings of ice and rock.

title: Uranus
d: Uranus rolls around the Sun on its side, tipped 98 degrees, likely from an ancient collision. Methane gives it a pale blue-green color, and despite its dista...
description: Uranus rolls around the Sun on its side, tipped 98 degrees, likely from an ancient collision. Methane gives it a pale blue-green color, and despite its distance it holds the coldest planetary atmosphere at -224 C. diameter: 50,724 km. distance: 19.2 AU. day: 17.2 hours. year: 84 years. moons: 28. note: Tipped on its side; coldest atmosphere..

facts.note: Tipped on its side; coldest atmosphere.

title: Neptune
d: Neptune was found by mathematics before any telescope saw it, predicted from wobbles in Uranus orbit. It is the windiest world known, with supersonic storms ...
description: Neptune was found by mathematics before any telescope saw it, predicted from wobbles in Uranus orbit. It is the windiest world known, with supersonic storms reaching 2,100 km/h across its deep blue methane atmosphere. diameter: 49,244 km. distance: 30.1 AU. day: 16.1 hours. year: 164.8 years. moons: 16. note: Windiest world; found by mathematics..

title: Ceres
d: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet of the inner solar system. NASA Dawn found bright salt deposits and hints of an an...
description: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet of the inner solar system. NASA Dawn found bright salt deposits and hints of an ancient subsurface ocean. diameter: 940 km. distance: 2.77 AU. note: Largest asteroid-belt object; visited by Dawn..

facts.note: Largest asteroid-belt object; visited by Dawn.

title: Pluto
d: Pluto surprised everyone when New Horizons flew by in 2015: a heart-shaped nitrogen glacier, ice mountains, and a thin blue atmosphere. It has five moons, th...
description: Pluto surprised everyone when New Horizons flew by in 2015: a heart-shaped nitrogen glacier, ice mountains, and a thin blue atmosphere. It has five moons, the largest, Charon, nearly half its size. diameter: 2,377 km. distance: 39.5 AU. note: Heart-shaped glacier; visited by New Horizons 2015..

facts.note: Heart-shaped glacier; visited by New Horizons 2015.

title: Haumea
d: Haumea spins once every 4 hours, stretching it into an egg shape, and it even hosts its own thin ring — a first for a dwarf planet.
description: Haumea spins once every 4 hours, stretching it into an egg shape, and it even hosts its own thin ring — a first for a dwarf planet. diameter: ~1,632 km. distance: 43.3 AU. note: Egg-shaped from fast spin; has a ring..

facts.note: Egg-shaped from fast spin; has a ring.

d: Makemake is one of the brightest Kuiper belt objects, coated in methane ice that gives it a reddish tint.
description: Makemake is one of the brightest Kuiper belt objects, coated in methane ice that gives it a reddish tint. diameter: ~1,430 km. distance: 45.7 AU. note: Bright methane-ice surface.. Checked against standard scientific references (IUPAC, NIST, NASA, and standard textbooks).

title: Eris
d: Eris is slightly smaller than Pluto but more massive, and its 2005 discovery forced astronomers to define planet — reclassifying Pluto.
description: Eris is slightly smaller than Pluto but more massive, and its 2005 discovery forced astronomers to define planet — reclassifying Pluto. diameter: 2,326 km. distance: 68 AU. note: Its discovery led to Pluto reclassification..

facts.note: Its discovery led to Pluto reclassification.

title: Moon
d: The Moon is the fifth-largest moon in the solar system and the only world humans have walked on. Its gravity steadies Earth axial tilt and drives the tides.
description: The Moon is the fifth-largest moon in the solar system and the only world humans have walked on. Its gravity steadies Earth axial tilt and drives the tides. diameter: 3,474 km. orbits: Earth. note: Stabilizes Earth seasons; visited by Apollo crews..

facts.note: Stabilizes Earth seasons; visited by Apollo crews.

title: Io
d: Io is the most volcanic world known, with hundreds of erupting sulfurous volcanoes resurfacing it constantly under Jupiter immense tidal squeezing.
description: Io is the most volcanic world known, with hundreds of erupting sulfurous volcanoes resurfacing it constantly under Jupiter immense tidal squeezing. diameter: 3,643 km. orbits: Jupiter. note: Most volcanic body known..

title: Europa
d: Europa hides a salty ocean beneath its cracked ice shell that may hold twice the water of all Earth oceans — a prime target in the search for life.
description: Europa hides a salty ocean beneath its cracked ice shell that may hold twice the water of all Earth oceans — a prime target in the search for life. diameter: 3,122 km. orbits: Jupiter. note: Subsurface ocean may hold twice Earth water..

facts.note: Subsurface ocean may hold twice Earth water.

title: Ganymede
d: Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system, bigger than Mercury, and the only moon known to generate its own magnetic field.
description: Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system, bigger than Mercury, and the only moon known to generate its own magnetic field. diameter: 5,268 km. orbits: Jupiter. note: Largest moon; bigger than Mercury..

title: Callisto
d: Callisto is the most heavily cratered body known, its surface a 4-billion-year record of impacts, possibly hiding a deep ocean.
description: Callisto is the most heavily cratered body known, its surface a 4-billion-year record of impacts, possibly hiding a deep ocean. diameter: 4,821 km. orbits: Jupiter. note: Most cratered body; ancient surface..

title: Titan
d: Titan has a thicker atmosphere than Earth and rain-fed lakes of liquid methane — the only other world with stable surface liquid and a full weather cycle.
description: Titan has a thicker atmosphere than Earth and rain-fed lakes of liquid methane — the only other world with stable surface liquid and a full weather cycle. diameter: 5,150 km. orbits: Saturn. note: Thick nitrogen atmosphere; methane lakes..

title: Enceladus
d: Enceladus blasts plumes of salty water from its south pole, feeding Saturn E ring; Cassini flew through them and tasted an ocean.
description: Enceladus blasts plumes of salty water from its south pole, feeding Saturn E ring; Cassini flew through them and tasted an ocean. diameter: 504 km. orbits: Saturn. note: Geysers spray ocean water into space..

facts.note: Geysers spray ocean water into space.

title: Rhea
d: Rhea is Saturn second-largest moon, a bright icy world of ancient craters.

d: Iapetus is the yin-yang moon: one hemisphere dark as coal, the other bright as snow, split by a giant equatorial ridge.
description: Iapetus is the yin-yang moon: one hemisphere dark as coal, the other bright as snow, split by a giant equatorial ridge. diameter: 1,470 km. orbits: Saturn. note: Two-toned: one side dark, one bright..

title: Triton
d: Triton orbits Neptune backwards, likely a captured Kuiper belt world, and erupts nitrogen geysers through its pink ice crust.
description: Triton orbits Neptune backwards, likely a captured Kuiper belt world, and erupts nitrogen geysers through its pink ice crust. diameter: 2,707 km. orbits: Neptune. note: Orbits backwards; nitrogen geysers..

title: Charon
d: Charon is so large relative to Pluto that the two orbit a point in space between them — a true binary world with red polar caps.
description: Charon is so large relative to Pluto that the two orbit a point in space between them — a true binary world with red polar caps. diameter: 1,212 km. orbits: Pluto. note: Half Pluto size; a true binary pair..

d: Phobos is a lumpy captured asteroid slowly spiraling inward; in tens of millions of years it will shatter into a ring around Mars.
